mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a recession.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained acceleration in real GDP growth above 3% quarter-over-quarter for two consecutive quarters indicates strengthening aggregate demand, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 q-o-q growth > 3% for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than baseline during periods of confirmed GDP acceleration, or the relationship inverts during high inflation episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE remains below 5% for three months, or the effect is absent during periods of strong productivity growth.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in the industrial production index below its previous 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which depresses earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of confirmed industrial production contraction, or the effect reverses in the presence of strong export demand.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both real personal income (PAYEMS) and consumer spending proxy (RSAFS) by more than 2% month-over-month signals robust household demand, which boosts corporate revenue and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and RSAFS rise >2% MoM, or the relationship breaks down during periods of high inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% over six months signals a disinflationary easing cycle, which lowers real interest rates and supports higher equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS falls >0.5% AND CPIAUCSL falls >0.5% over 6 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during coordinated FEDFUNDS and CPI declines, or the effect reverses during a credit crunch.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months signals a deepening recession, which reduces corporate earnings and increases default risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 8% for two months, or the effect is absent during periods of fiscal stimulus.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals strengthening residential demand, which boosts construction and related sector earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average for 5 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during sustained HOUST strength above its moving average, or the effect reverses during a mortgage rate spike.
